DBAP 5010.title: Introduction to Applied Business Research
DBAP 5010.description: This course explores the fundamental issues in business research, including the purpose of business research, the role business research plays in helping managers in decision making, the process involved in the scientific inquiry applied to business including identifying interesting and practically significant research questions, deducing testable hypotheses, conducting systematic research using appropriate methodology, drawing conclusions, and making theoretical and practical contributions. Practical and ethical issues involved in conducting business research will also be discussed.
cilos: Explain the purpose of applied business research and think critically about business research.
Describe the process of conducting applied business research.
Identify commonly used research methods in applied business research.
Apply the basic practical skills of conducting business research (e.g., literature review).
Recognize the ethical issues involved in conducting applied business research.

DBAP 5020.title: Applied Statistics and Regression
DBAP 5020.description: The course introduces various applications of statistics in business, in particular, regression analysis and its applications. The main topics to be covered include data exploration methods, inference, and regression.
cilos: Apply appropriate data analysis tools (data exploration methods and regression) to conduct sound data analysis.
Use statistical software such as R to do estimation, modeling, and forecasting.

DBAP 5030.title: Survey Research
DBAP 5030.description: This course provides an introduction to survey research with a focus on its applications in business research. Students will gain the knowledge and skills needed to design and conduct surveys, analyze survey data, and apply survey research methods.
cilos: Develop testable research propositions.
Formulate hypotheses based on these propositions.
Identify the research methods relevant to these hypotheses.
Design surveys to test research hypotheses.
Analyze preliminary data from surveys research and draw valid conclusions.

DBAP 5040.title: Qualitative Research Method in Business
DBAP 5040.description: Qualitative research is critical in inducting novel theory, and elaborating existing theory with frame-breaking insights. It is particularly suited to answer the "how" question, enabling students to understand the process underlying the phenomenon and hence develop better insights into the mechanisms. This course will cover when and how to conduct inductive multiple case research, focusing on specific skills such as how to identify a research question that fits multiple case research, craft a rigorous research design, use theoretical sampling, gain access to companies, collect data and write research cases, conduct within- and cross- case comparisons, and finally induce generalizable insights that make a genuine theoretical contribution.
cilos: Conduct and evaluate inductive multiple case research.
Identify a research question that fits multiple case research.
Craft a rigorous research design for multiple case research.
Analyze trade-offs among different data collection methods.
Conduct within- and cross-case comparisons.

DBAP 5050.title: Experimental Designs
DBAP 5050.description: This course focuses on experimental research methods in the field of business. It provides students with an introduction to the tools and techniques necessary for collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and evaluating experimental data.
cilos: Identify interesting and relevant research questions.
Formulate hypotheses based on these research questions.
Identify the research methods relevant to these hypotheses.
Design experiments to test research hypotheses.
Analyze preliminary data from experimental research and draw valid conclusions.

DBAP 5060.title: Economics Foundation for Applied Business Research
DBAP 5060.description: This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of applied microeconomic theory at the DBA level. Through rigorous training of key concepts and methodologies, students will develop the skills necessary to comprehend, analyze, and construct theoretical models in various business contexts. The course will delve into foundational topics such as consumer theory, game theory, and industrial organization. Topics covered under industrial organization include information economics, classical models of competition among firms, and platform competition. Emphasis will be placed on practical applications of theoretical frameworks in business research.
cilos: Be well acquainted with foundation economics knowledge helpful to their studies and research in noneconomics areas.
Build theoretical models that capture strategic interactions in business settings.
Apply the foundation knowledge to conduct independent research in economic fields such as game theory or industrial organization.

DBAP 5110.title: Frontiers in Accounting Research
DBAP 5110.description: This course introduces students to accounting research. It covers the frontier accounting research topics such as financial accounting, international accounting, accounting for corporate governance and auditing.
cilos: Explain concepts and issues in recent financial accounting research.
Explain concepts and issues in recent auditing research.
Apply concepts of financial accounting and auditing to address issues in corporate governance.
Compare and contrast financial accounting and auditing systems in different countries.
Present financial accounting and auditing research that has practical implications.

DBAP 5120.title: Frontiers in Economics Research
DBAP 5120.description: This course introduces students to frontier topics in economics research relevant for business, including topics such as innovation, globalization (trade and FDI), personnel management, industrial organization, competition, and digital economy.
cilos: Identify the latest economics research on timely, cutting-edge topics.
Compare and contrast the research methods and quality of evidence in economics research.
Identify how economics research has contributed to business design, management, and practice.
Conceptualize and design economics research to address selected business problems.
Present professional research and articulate its significance.

DBAP 5130.title: Frontiers in Finance Research
DBAP 5130.description: This course introduces major finance research areas to students: asset pricing and investment theories and practice, corporate finance issues, microstructure studies, and financial derivatives pricing and strategies. For each area, the basic issues and currently prevalent views will be presented.
cilos: Define the subareas of finance research and the central questions in these subareas.
Explore specific topics of interest as a potential research direction.
Identify the areas of research strength of the Finance Department.

DBAP 5140.title: Frontiers in Information Systems Research
DBAP 5140.description: This course introduces students to information systems research in terms of the intersection between technology, society, organization, people, and policy. It analyzes frontier IS research topics such as online social media, digital platforms and competitions, and network strategy and economics.
cilos: Synthesize the latest IS research on timely topics such as online social media, digital platforms and competitions, and network strategy and economics.
Compare and contrast the research methods and quality of evidence in different IS research.
Identify how IS research has contributed to business design, management, and practice.
Conceptualize and design proper IS research to address selected business or social problems.
Present professional IS research and articulate its significance.

DBAP 5150.title: Frontiers in Operations Management Research
DBAP 5150.description: This course surveys the current operations management research topics that are of interest to senior business executives. The topics may change every year.
cilos: Identify the current research topics in operations management.
Recognize how research can improve business practices in operations management.
Develop and apply the skills to identify interesting research problems in operations management.

DBAP 5160.title: Frontiers in Management Research
DBAP 5160.description: This introductory course exposes students to the latest research and trends in management research (e.g., organizational behavior, human resources management, strategic management, international business, entrepreneurship, and business ethics). Students will read and critique latest research papers from selected topics and participate in class discussion. Students are expected to understand management issues of current and future concerns, identify an interesting and practically important frontier research question in a management topic of choice, and write an executable research proposal to address the question.
cilos: Recognize the latest research and trends in strategy and organization.
Recognize the latest research and trends in organizational behavior and human resource management.
Articulate current business and organizational issues relevant to the management field.
Develop independent scholarly research on a topic of choice in the management field.
Apply the latest research and knowledge in management in their business settings.

DBAP 5170.title: Frontiers in Marketing Research
DBAP 5170.description: This course introduces students to the latest research topics in marketing and covers recent marketing research findings from several different research paradigms.
cilos: Identify the latest research topics in marketing.
Define the different research paradigms involved in marketing research.
Assess the quality of academic marketing research and relate it to business practice.
Conceptualize and design research questions in marketing.
Present the latest marketing research and articulate its significance.

DBAP 5210.title: Research in Financial Accounting
DBAP 5210.description: This course introduces students to the use of research methods in economics, finance, and statistics to examine important financial accounting issues.
cilos: Compare and contrast the concepts of earnings and cash Flows.
Compare and contrast earnings management using accrual and real activities.
Define companies’ voluntary disclosure.
Recognize the impact of mandatory disclosure regulation on corporate practice.
Apply the concept of market efficiency to fundamental analysis in equity investment.
Identify the role of financial Intermediaries in accounting.
Present professional accounting research in financial accounting.

DBAP 5220.title: Research on Managerial Accounting, Corporate Governance, and Executive Compensation
DBAP 5220.description: This course involves discussion of research in managerial accounting, corporate governance and executive compensation. Use of research tools in economics, finance and statistics to examine important accounting issues in the above areas will be covered.
cilos: Describe the association between corporate board structures and accounting.
Describe the association between corporate ownership structures and accounting.
Describe the association between the incentives of executives and accounting.
Describe the association between debt contracts and accounting.
Identify the current research on managerial accounting, corporate governance, and executive compensation.
Explain the impact of regulation on managerial accounting, corporate governance, and executive compensation.
Explain the impact of litigation on managerial accounting, corporate governance, and Executive Compensation.
Present professional accounting research in managerial accounting, corporate governance, and executive compensation.

DBAP 5310.title: Business Economics: Strategic and Behavioral Approach
DBAP 5310.description: This course uses economic analysis to examine a selection of topics of importance to business management. Topics may include demand analysis, pricing strategies, game theory and applications, asymmetric information, agency theory and applications, organization economics, and mergers and acquisitions.
cilos: Apply demand and supply analysis in predicting market price and dynamics.
Analyze key trade-offs in pricing and conduct research on pricing strategies.
Formulate strategic decisions using game theoretic methods to address challenges in competitive markets.
Apply economic thinking and tools for organization design.
Communicate economic research and analysis to multiple stakeholder groups.

DBAP 5320.title: Empirical Methods for Economic Analysis
DBAP 5320.description: This course teaches empirical approaches and methods commonly used in applied economic research, including discussion of actual applications to business problems. Topics include identification strategies, regression specification, panel data methods, event studies, program evaluation, and instrumental variables.
cilos: Recognize fundamental problems in identifying causal relationships and the strengths and weaknesses of different identification strategies.
Choose appropriate regression specifications that best fit the data and address identification concerns.
Adopt appropriate methods to exploit the advantages of panel data.
Apply specific identification strategies, including event studies, diff-in-diffs, and instrumental variables.
Communicate economic research and analysis to multiple stakeholder groups.

DBAP 5410.title: Asset Allocation and Portfolio Analysis
DBAP 5410.description: This course begins with the central idea of asset pricing theory regarding risk-return trade-off and continues with asset allocation decisions and modern portfolio theories. Using primary asset markets of stocks and bonds as the battle ﬁeld, it presents concepts and methodologies of identifying market-wide factors and factor betas as measures of risks and risk exposures. It also discusses popular trading strategies of capturing alphas associated with ﬁrm-speciﬁc attributes.
cilos: Explain the notion of diversification and the mean-variance optimization framework.
Explain the notions of diversifiable risk, undiversifiable risk, risk return trade-off and Sharpe ratio.
Assess the difference between  efficient market hypothesis and behavioral theory.
Recognize popular trading strategies of capturing alphas associated with firm-specific attributes.

DBAP 5420.title: Fixed-income Strategies
DBAP 5420.description: This course focuses on ﬁxed income markets and presents strategies dealing with interest rate risk and credit risk. For the former, arbitrage based and equilibrium based theoretical models will be briefed and empirical models using key yields and macroeconomic factors will be discussed at length. For the latter, structural models and reduced-form models will be taught, the popular strategies used by ﬁrms and institutions will be explained, and lessons learned from recent ﬁnancial crises will be discussed.
cilos: Explain the notion of interest rate risk and credit risk.
Identify the methodology of modeling interest rate risk and credit risk.
Set up models for analyzing specific issues.
Implement models using data to tackle real questions.

DBAP 5430.title: Financial Derivatives and Risk Management
DBAP 5430.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of how ﬁnancial derivatives are priced and used in hedging, speculation and arbitrage. The discussion on derivatives pricing begins with no-arbitrage based pricing theories, continues with equilibrium based pricing theories, and ends with empirical evidence on these models, with special emphasis on the informational roles of derivatives.
cilos: Describe the notion of complete market and the methodology of no-arbitrage pricing.
Assess the performance of various pricing models and the limitation of no-arbitrage pricing.
Extract information contained in options.
Implement models using data to tackle real questions.

DBAP 5440.title: Behavioral Finance
DBAP 5440.description: Many careful observational studies of actual behavior – and at least three recent Nobel Prizes – suggest that the standard economic paradigm of rational investors in an efficient market does not adequately describe real-world behavior. Behavioral finance combines findings in cognitive psychology with conventional economic logic to provide alternative explanations of such observed behavior. We will examine how psychology of decision making under uncertainty affects the traditional paradigm, while paying attention to practical applications for portfolio and investment management.
cilos: Understand how to apply psychology in financial markets.
Identify the methodologies used in the recent literature to study applications.
Formulate important research questions relating concepts taught in class to students’ personal experience.

DBAP 5450.title: Green Finance
DBAP 5450.description: Green finance is the use of financial tools to improve environmental outcomes. The course begins with the valuation of financial assets with non-pecuniary preference, continues on various approaches to addressing the issues in green finance, and examines development in financial instruments such as green bonds and carbon credits.
cilos: Understand the issues related to environmental economics and finance.
Familiarize with standard methodologies used in theoretical and empirical studies of green finance.
Use available environment-related databases.
Formulate problems of their interest in green finance.
Solve problems of their interest in green finance.

DBAP 5510.title: Information Systems Research in Business
DBAP 5510.description: This course surveys state-of-the-art information systems research related to business analysis, design, and practice. The course will provide students with a broad coverage of how research into IS and technology management uncovers new insights and drives innovative business practices.
cilos: Evaluate IS impacts in business analysis, design, and practice.
Discuss impacts of IS on individuals, organizations, and/or society.
Evaluate research approach and methodology for conducting IS research in different business settings.
Identify IS research gaps and opportunities in business analysis, design, and practice.
Develop and present comprehensive IS research proposal (research questions, theory, methodology, potential impacts).

DBAP 5520.title: Information Systems Theories
DBAP 5520.description: This course reviews information systems (IS) theories and their applications in businesses and the society. The course will provide students with fundamental knowledge and insights on exemplary IS theories applied to various topics, such as technology adoption, knowledge management, crowdsourcing, crowdfunding, digital platforms, electronic commerce, user-generated content, social media analytics, information privacy, IT security, etc.
cilos: Identify the role of theory in IS research, describe what theory is and how to make a theoretical contribution.
Explain the theories used in IS research on various topics, e.g., technology adoption, knowledge management, crowdsourcing, digital platforms, privacy, IT security, etc.
Compare and contrast the IS theories and quality of evidence in different IS research.
Identify how IS theories has contributed to business design, management and practice.
Conceptualize and design proper IS research to address selected business or social problem.
Present professional IS research and articulate its significance.

DBAP 5530.title: AI in Business
DBAP 5530.description: This course explores the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the business landscape. Designed for DBA students, it covers key AI concepts, technologies, and applications relevant to various industries. Students will learn how to leverage AI tools for decision-making, improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and drive innovation. The curriculum includes topics such as machine learning, natural language processing, data analytics, and ethical considerations in AI deployment. By the end of the course, students will gain an understanding of AI and identify related business issues that could become a potential topic of their thesis research.
cilos: Demonstrate a clear understanding of key AI concepts, technologies, and methodologies relevant to business applications.
Analyze and interpret data using AI tools, enabling informed decision-making based on data-driven insights.
Develop strategies for integrating AI into business processes to enhance efficiency and competitiveness.
Recognize and evaluate ethical issues related to the use of AI in business, including privacy, bias, and accountability.
Identify potential research questions in studying AI-related issues.
Cultivate a mindset for innovation, exploring how AI can create new business opportunities and models.
Effectively communicate AI concepts and their business implications to diverse stakeholders.

DBAP 5610.title: Supply Chain Management
DBAP 5610.description: This course will provide students with fundamental knowledge in operations management and supply chain management, focusing on topics related to the management of business process that produce and deliver goods or services in a global business environment. Topics include process analysis and improvement, inventory and revenue management, supply chain strategies, supply chain integration and coordination, and other important issues.
cilos: Explain the importance of processes and operational excellence in modern organizations.
Achieve operations and service  improvement by applying operations and supply chain management theories into practice.
Apply a set of key approaches for business practitioners to improve operations and supply chain activities for better business decision making.

DBAP 5620.title: Research Methodology in Operations and Supply Chain Management
DBAP 5620.description: This course will provide methodology training for students to conduct research in the Operations Management and Supply Chain Management areas. Major topics include deterministic optimization models, applied probability models, simulation, and empirical methods.
cilos: Identify basic methodology in conducting research in OM and supply chain areas.
Use the methodology for solving applied research problems.

DBAP 5710.title: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management
DBAP 5710.description: This course exposes students to major theories and research topics in organizational behavior and human resource management with the aim of promoting individual, team and organizational effectiveness. Sample topics include individual differences (e.g., personality, attitudes, and moods), judgement and decision making, creativity and innovation, negotiation, team effectiveness, conflict management, leadership, organizational culture, recruitment, selection, performance management, training and development, and compensation. Students will read and critique selected research papers from selected topics and participate in class discussion. At the end of the course, students are expected to develop a good and comprehensive understanding of organizational behavior and human resource management research, identify an interesting and practically important research question in a topic of choice, and write an executable research proposal to address the question.
cilos: Identify and apply up-to-date and in-depth knowledge of OBHR literature.
Recognize and explain contemporary business and organizational issues related to OBHR.
Develop independent substantive scholarly research in OBHR.
Apply latest research in OBHR to their business and organizational settings.

DBAP 5720.title: Strategic Management and Organization Theory
DBAP 5720.description: This course exposes students to major theoretical foundations and topics in strategic management and organization theory with the aim of promoting effective strategic decision making, execution, and organizations that promote ﬁrm performance and interests of various stakeholders. Students are expected to develop a good and comprehensive understanding of strategy research, identify an interesting and practically important research question in a topic of choice, and write an executable research proposal to address the question.
cilos: Describe the nature and development of organizational theories.
Define the theories on firm competitive advantages.
Identify deep linkage between firm transaction cost and the decisions of making, buying or allying.
Identify the role of social networks.
Explain corporate governance with agency theory.
Explain the behavioral perspective of firms.
Analyze firm actions under uncertainty.
Analyze firms in a broad institutional environment.

DBAP 5730.title: ESG and Sustainability Research: Management and Organization Foundations
DBAP 5730.description: The share of executives, board members, and investment managers who consider governance, climate risk, and other ESG issues as well as stakeholders’ opinions of the firm to be material to their business decisions has risen dramatically. This course exposes students to major theoretical foundations and topics in corporate governance and social responsibility with the aim of promoting effective strategic decision-making, execution, and organizations that consider the interests of various stakeholders. Students are expected to develop a good and comprehensive understanding of corporate governance and social responsibility research, identify an interesting and practically important research question in a topic of choice, and write an executable research proposal to address the question.
cilos: Understand the latest management research on ESG, sustainability, and related cutting-edge topics.
Compare and contrast the research methods and quality of evidence in ESG and sustainability research.
Conceptualize and design ESG and sustainability research to address selected management challenges.

DBAP 5810.title: Information Processing for Marketing Strategy
DBAP 5810.description: This course provides an overview of topics in psychology and consumer behavior research. An information processing approach is used to help students get familiar with a range of diverse topics such as attitude formation and change, culture, information processing, motivation and goals, emotion, and consumer decision making. Practical applications of these topics as related to marketing issues and the implications for marketing managers will also be discussed.
cilos: Recognize the latest research topics in Information Processing relevant for Marketing.
Explain the different conceptual paradigms involved in information processing research.
Assess the quality of psychology research and relate it to marketing practice.
Conceptualize and design research questions in information processing.
Present latest research on consumer information processing and articulate its significance.

DBAP 5820.title: Behavioral Decision Making for Business Research
DBAP 5820.description: This course is designed to familiarize students with a wide variety of issues related to consumer and managerial judgment and decision making. Given the emphasis of the course on behavioral decision making, the topics covered pertain mainly to descriptive rather than normative aspects of decision making. The contents will be useful for researchers in many fields of business such as marketing, economics, finance, and management.
cilos: Identify the classic and contemporary literature in the area of behavioral decision making.
Translate these findings to appropriate business settings.
Formulate hypotheses based on this literature that can be tested in applied business settings.
Design appropriate tests of research hypotheses in field settings.
Propose a translational application of cutting-edge behavioral research to a contemporary business issue.

DBAP 5830.title: Managing Customers in the Digital Economy
DBAP 5830.description: This course introduces students to academic research on customer management in the digital economy. The course draws on both economics and psychology principles and relies on empirical, analytical, and experimental methods.
cilos: Familiarize with economic and psychological theories commonly used in customer management, including the drivers of customer loyalty, and key methodologies.
Learn the key activities and concepts in customer management, such as customer acquisition and retention, customer equity, customer lifetime value, etc.
Understand the evolution of marketing practices in customer management, including loyalty programs, customization, pricing personalization, referral programs, and social media.

Identify the stakeholders in customer management, including external partners (e.g., distribution channel), competitors, internal partners in a multi-divisional company, and regulators (e.g., on privacy), and discuss the challenges and opportunities in managing the relationship with
respective stakeholders.

DBAP 6000.title: Special Topics
DBAP 6000.description: This course intends to explore an array of business research topics important to DBA students. Students may repeat the course for credit as long as the topics covered are different.
cilos: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of the concepts and theories on various business research topics.
Apply appropriate research methodologies and tools to analyze and interpret research findings.
Apply frameworks and concepts of the topics concerned to address business challenges.
Communicate key findings precisely and concisely through written reports.
Develop a deeper understanding of the complexities of emerging business research topics.

DBAP 6100.title: Independent Study
DBAP 6100.description: Study of selected business issues under the supervision of a faculty member. The course may be repeated for credit to satisfy the program requirements of the DBA Program. (Special permission from the Academic Director is required for students to take this course.)
cilos: Conduct an independent study on a selected topic of a business issue or practice.
Apply frameworks and concepts learned from the program to address the business challenges.
Apply an interdisciplinary approach in reviewing the latest developments of the chosen topic.
Analyze and communicate key findings precisely and concisely through a written report.

DBAP 6200.title: DBA Research Proposal Preparation
DBAP 6200.description: This course will help students to get familiar with literature in the chosen research area, identify appropriate topics for thesis research, and prepare detailed thesis proposals through independent study under the supervision of faculty members. Maybe graded PP.
cilos: Finalize their thesis research topics.
Get familiar with related literature in the chosen research area.
Identify problems and areas for improvement for their thesis research.
Work out a detailed plan for completing the research.
Complete their research proposals.

DBAP 6300.title: DBA Residential Program
DBAP 6300.description: Students will conduct research under the supervision of their faculty advisors. Students need to be on campus for one to two days for research activities in each regular term. In addition, there should be at least 10 contact hours with the advisors during the term. Graded P or F.
cilos: Integrate acquired knowledge and skills in conducting applied research.
Apply effective communication and time management skills.
Demonstrate significant progress in their thesis research.

DBAP 7980.title: DBA Thesis Research
DBAP 7980.description: Original and independent DBA research. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. Graded PP, P or F.
cilos: Design, develop, and conduct research in an applied research area.
Apply research methodologies in formulating business solutions.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
